newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: BIL to focus on costs, private bank, euro.
newsitem.headline: BIL to focus on costs, private bank, euro.

text.p: Andre Roelants, new chief executive officer of Banque Internationale a Luxembourg (BIL), said that his first priorities are cutting costs, boosting asset management activities and preparing for the euro.

"The first big parameter we have to work on is costs. We must cut our cost/income ratio further," Roelants told Reuters in an interview at a seminar about the future of the Luxembourg financial markets organised by Belgian financial daily L'Echo.

Roelants, who succeeded Jean Krier at the start of the year, said he wants to cut BIL's cost/income ratio, currently at 54 percent on a consolidated basis, to 50 percent by year-end and 45 percent by 1999.
Part of this move should come from a stronger focus on private banking and asset management activities, which are already a mainstay of Luxembourg banks.

Private banking activities contributed about 38 percent of BIL's 1995 gross pre-tax profit; its universal bank activities in Luxembourg about 25 percent. The rest came in equal parts from institutional activities (fund management) and capital markets trading.
BIL earned a 2.85 billion Luxembourg franc ($84.4 million) consolidated net profit in 1995 and expects to earn about 3.1 billion in 1996.

Belgian-born Roelants said that in the mutual fund business, he also wants to focus more on asset management, rather than administrative management. Like many Luxembourg banks, BIL is very active in fund administration activities, such as calculating intrinsic values, registering shareholders and acting as a paying agent.
Roelants said that the alliance of his parent company Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet (CCB) with French Credit Local de France last year should have little impact on BIL.
"For CCB we are a diversification of their activites," he said, adding that BIL had worked on a few capital market operations for CLF in recent months.
One major challenge will be the preparation for the single European currency in 1999, which is expected to wipe out the market in Eurobonds for the currencies that join it.
Like most Luxembourg banks, BIL is very active in Eurobonds -- bonds issued outside the issuer's home market.
Roelants said the introduction of the euro will lead to bigger issues on the Eurobond market, as the big lenders will try to cut costs by inflating the size of their loans.
He said the average issue will swell from the current $100-200 million to $400-500 million or more.
"In that area, our competition will not consist of the local Luxembourg banks, but of the really big players," he said.
But he added there would always be issuers in the $100 million category.

In preparation for the euro, BIL has boosted its activities in Ecu-bond issuance to 800 million Ecu (around 31 billion francs) in 1996 from virtually zero in 1995. He added that he expects BIL to be book runner for 35-40 billion francs' worth of Ecu bonds in 1997.
"We want to show the market that we can do more than just Luxembourg-franc denominated Eurobonds," he said.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710 ($ = 33.78 Luxembourg Francs)
